title: [Bug]: LinearBase.load_weights substitutes the module for a missing parameter, surfacing as a confusing AttributeError
body:
### Your current environment

0.27.1
env - doesn't mater for this

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In `LinearBase.load_weights` the lookup falls back to `self` when the parameter does not exist:

```python
param: Parameter
if "." in name:
    submodule, _, attr = name.rpartition(".")
    param = getattr(self.get_submodule(submodule), attr, self)
```

`self` is the *module*, not a `Parameter`, so the annotation one line above is violated. Loading then proceeds and fails several frames later inside the module's own `weight_loader`:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 732, in weight_loader
    param_data = param.data
AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'
```

Nothing in that message names the tensor that could not be resolved.

**Repro:** load a quantized DFlash2 draft model (compressed-tensors FP8, `strategy: channel`). `qwen3_dflash.py` fuses q/k/v and gate/up through explicit per-name entries (`".q_proj": (".qkv_proj", "q")`) and defines no `stacked_params_mapping`, so `...mlp.gate_proj.weight_scale` does not resolve, the module is substituted, and the error above appears instead of "no such parameter".

**Patch** — keeps the fallback, refuses to load into a non-parameter:

```diff
             if param is None and name == "bias":
                 continue
+            if not isinstance(param, torch.nn.Parameter):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{self.prefix}: cannot load {name!r} — no such parameter, "
+                    f"got {type(param).__name__} instead. This usually means the "
+                    f"checkpoint carries a tensor the layer does not declare, e.g. a "
+                    f"quantization scale on a layer built without a quant_config."
+                )
             param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id)
```

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
